questions.stem: A client taking clozapine for 6 weeks calls the clinic with fever, chills, and a new sore throat. Which nursing response best reflects current FDA safety guidance?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Reassure the client that infection symptoms are expected during early clozapine therapy and can be reviewed at the next scheduled psychiatric visit.","B":"Arrange prompt clinical evaluation and an ANC because infection symptoms can signal clozapine-associated neutropenia, which remains a serious risk.","C":"Tell the client to stop all laboratory monitoring because the federal clozapine REMS program was removed and blood counts are no longer useful.","D":"Advise the client to continue clozapine unchanged for several days and seek evaluation only if a widespread rash or facial swelling develops."}}
questions.rationale: FDA removed the clozapine REMS in 2025, but the risk of severe neutropenia remains. Current FDA guidance and prescribing information continue to support ANC monitoring, and infection symptoms such as fever, chills, or sore throat require prompt medical evaluation rather than routine follow-up.
questions.source_name: FDA — Clozapine REMS Removal and Neutropenia Safety Communication
questions.source_detail: REMS removed effective June 13, 2025; severe neutropenia risk remains and ANC monitoring continues under prescribing information.

questions.stem: A client with rheumatoid arthritis is prescribed oral methotrexate once weekly. Which additional teaching is most appropriate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Take methotrexate daily during a painful flare, then return to weekly dosing after symptoms improve because dose frequency can follow disease activity.","B":"Delay folate supplementation during the first month so methotrexate efficacy can be assessed before adding a vitamin that may reduce its therapeutic effect.","C":"Use folate only if mouth sores or gastrointestinal effects develop because preventive supplementation is unnecessary when baseline blood counts are normal.","D":"Take folic or folinic acid as directed with low-dose methotrexate to reduce selected adverse effects while keeping methotrexate on its weekly schedule."}}
questions.rationale: Current methotrexate labeling for rheumatoid arthritis uses once-weekly dosing and directs folic acid or folinic acid administration to reduce methotrexate adverse reactions. Daily substitution for a weekly regimen can be dangerous, and routine vitamin K supplementation is not part of standard low-dose methotrexate therapy.
questions.source_detail: Rheumatoid arthritis dosing is once weekly; administer folic acid or folinic acid to reduce adverse reactions.

questions.stem: A client takes levothyroxine each morning and also uses a calcium supplement with breakfast. Which instruction should the nurse reinforce?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach about 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast and separate it from calcium or other absorption-interfering products.","B":"Take levothyroxine with breakfast each morning but move the calcium supplement to bedtime because food does not meaningfully alter thyroid-hormone absorption.","C":"Take levothyroxine before breakfast together with calcium because calcium interferes mainly with iron-containing thyroid products rather than levothyroxine.","D":"Take levothyroxine after breakfast at the same time each day and separate calcium by two hours because consistent timing offsets food effects."}}
questions.rationale: Current levothyroxine labeling recommends a single daily dose on an empty stomach, about 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast, and separation by at least 4 hours from drugs known to interfere with absorption. Calcium products are a common absorption concern, so consistent timing and separation matter.
questions.source_detail: Single daily dose on an empty stomach 30–60 minutes before breakfast; separate absorption-interfering drugs by at least 4 hours.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old client who smokes 8 cigarettes per day and has migraine with aura requests a combined estrogen-progestin contraceptive. Which response is most accurate?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Combined hormonal contraception is category 1 because smoking fewer than 15 cigarettes per day removes the vascular restriction after age 35.","B":"Combined hormonal contraception is category 2 because migraine with aura is relevant only when hypertension is also uncontrolled or severe.","C":"Combined hormonal contraception should not be used because migraine with aura is category 4, and smoking at age 35 or older adds further vascular risk.","D":"Combined estrogen-progestin contraception is preferred because estrogen lowers stroke risk enough to offset the additional risk associated with smoking."}}
questions.rationale: CDC U.S. MEC classifies combined hormonal contraception as category 4 for migraine with aura, meaning an unacceptable health risk. Smoking at age 35 or older adds additional cardiovascular risk; for fewer than 15 cigarettes per day, smoking alone is category 3 for combined hormonal contraception.
questions.source_name: CDC — U.S. Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use, 2024
questions.source_detail: Migraine with aura: CHC category 4. Smoking age ≥35 and <15 cigarettes/day: CHC category 3.

questions.stem: A client who can become pregnant is starting isotretinoin and says, “I am not sexually active, so the pregnancy-prevention program does not apply to me.” Which response is most accurate in August 2026?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"You are exempt from iPLEDGE because FDA ended the isotretinoin pregnancy-safety program when it approved program changes in February 2026.","B":"Isotretinoin remains under iPLEDGE because of embryo-fetal toxicity; you must follow the program's current pregnancy-prevention and testing requirements.","C":"Only a pregnancy test after the final dose is required because FDA eliminated pretreatment pregnancy testing for every patient starting isotretinoin in 2026.","D":"iPLEDGE applies only to patients who report current sexual activity; documented abstinence automatically removes pregnancy-testing and program requirements."}}
questions.rationale: As of August 13, 2026, isotretinoin remains subject to the iPLEDGE REMS to mitigate embryo-fetal toxicity. FDA delayed implementation of the planned 2026 iPLEDGE modifications from August 8 to November 15, 2026. Current program requirements therefore still apply pending that implementation.
questions.source_name: FDA — iPLEDGE Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS)
questions.source_detail: FDA announced June 16, 2026 that planned modifications were delayed until November 15, 2026; iPLEDGE remains in effect for embryo-fetal risk mitigation.
